tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description: Create a get-paid invoice for the spend-key owner. Returns a /r/{publicId} URL. Another agent can call pay_invoice with that URL; a human opening the link sees Vybe crypto checkout. Does not move money and does not require Approve. After sharing, call get_invoice with the publicId to check if it was

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: Check whether an invoice you created is still pending or already paid. Pass the publicId or /r/ url from create_invoice. Use this before taking a follow-up action that should only run after payment. Only works for invoices owned by this spend key’s owner. Related: create_invoice, list_invoices.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: List invoices the spend-key owner created (open, paid, etc.). Use to find a publicId, then get_invoice for details. Related: create_invoice, get_invoice.

tools.name: pay_invoice
tools.description: Pay a Vybe invoice by /r/ URL or publicId under the owner’s spend key. Creates awaiting_approval — money does not move until Approve in Vybe. Only vybe.finance/r/… links are allowed (not arbitrary URLs). Friendship is not required. Related: create_invoice, get_invoice, get_limits, get_spend_balance,

tools.name: send_to_user
tools.description: Send USDC/USDT to a mutual friend. Pass username (@handle) when known, or name (first, last, or full name). Lookup is limited to mutual friends — never invent wallet addresses. If several friends match the name, the tool returns candidates; ask the owner which @username, then retry. Creates a pendin

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search the Vybe Marketplace for MCP tools the user can use: free tools (run with run_free_tool, no sign-in) and paid tools (pay per use with pay_offering). Use this when the user asks for a capability you do not have, e.g. reading a PDF, looking up a postcode or checking a crypto transaction. Return

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: Full details for one marketplace tool: actions with their inputs, an example, price, seller and health, plus the exact next step. For a paid tool the next step is pay_offering with its offeringUrl, then use_paid_offering with toolName and toolArguments. For a free tool it is run_free_tool, which nee

tools.name: run_free_tool
tools.description: Run a free tool from the Vybe Marketplace and get its answer. No sign-in or spend key needed, and nothing is charged. Get the slug, action names and inputs from search_tools or get_tool first. Free tools have fair-use limits per caller; if you hit one, tell the user when it resets. Paid tools can't

tools.name: pay_offering
tools.description: Start a Vybe Collect payment under the owner's connected spend key (OAuth Sign in or Bearer VAPT). Creates a pending pay and returns awaiting_approval — money does not move until the wallet owner taps Approve in Vybe (web or mobile). After paid (or trial), call use_paid_offering with the returned pu

tools.name: get_spend_balance
tools.description: Return the bound spend key’s policy headroom for the last 24 hours: daily remaining, pending, and paid. This is not the on-chain USDC wallet balance — use get_wallet_balance for that. Call this before pay_offering to check whether a pay would hit the daily cap. Related: get_wallet_balance, get_limit

tools.name: get_wallet_balance
tools.description: Read-only on-chain USDC/USDT balances for the spend key owner’s Vybe wallet (Base, Ethereum, BNB). Use this to tell the user how much they can spend. Separate from get_spend_balance (VAPT caps). Does not move funds. Related: get_spend_balance, get_limits, pay_offering.

tools.name: get_limits
tools.description: Return the bound spend key’s hard limits: label, per-transaction max in USD, daily cap, optional seller allowlist, expiry, and authMode (oauth or vapt). Use this to tell the user what the agent is allowed to request before calling pay_offering. Related: get_spend_balance, get_wallet_balance.

tools.name: list_recent_pays
tools.description: List recent Collect pays, friend sends, and invoice pays started by the bound spend key, newest first. Filter by status: pending (waiting on Approve), paid (settled), or all. For paid Collect rows, call use_paid_offering with publicId. Related: pay_offering, pay_invoice, send_to_user, use_paid_offer

tools.name: use_paid_offering
tools.description: After a Collect pay is settled (status paid or trial), use this tool with the publicId from pay_offering. It branches by offering type: research/asset returns the file; MCP lists seller tools (omit toolName) or runs one (pass toolName + toolArguments); API proxies method+path(+body) through Vybe. Pr

tools.name: fetch_paid_content
tools.description: Unlock research/file offerings only. For MCP or API offerings, call use_paid_offering with the same publicId instead. Related: use_paid_offering, pay_offering.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "pay_offering" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_limits" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "pay" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_invoice, get_invoice, get_tool · Private data: send_to_user, pay_offering, get_spend_balance, get_wallet_balance, use_paid_offering, fetch_paid_content · Public sink: send_to_user · Destructive: get_invoice, search_tools, run_free_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_invoice, get_invoice, get_tool · Private data: send_to_user, pay_offering, get_spend_balance, get_wallet_balance, use_paid_offering, fetch_paid_content · Public sink: send_to_user · Destructive: get_invoice, search_tools, run_free_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
